newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-WESTERN AUSTRALIA GRAB FIRST INNINGS LEAD.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WESTERN AUSTRALIA GRAB FIRST INNINGS LEAD.

text.p: Sheffield Shield leaders Western Australia guaranteed themselves two points by taking a first innings lead in the match against Queensland on Sunday.
Western Australia, who went into the game four points clear of Tasmania, dismissed Queensland for 400 in reply to their first innings 414.
But Queensland struck a blow late in the day by removing opener Mike Hussey for one to leave Western Australia on three for one at the close of the third day at the WACA Ground.
Resuming on 162 for two, Queensland built their total around half centuries by Matthew Mott, Jimmy Maher and Geoff Foley.
But they lost their last five wickets for 73 as Western Australia captain Tom Moody captured four for 73.
Under Shield rules, Western Australia will keep the two points for a first innings lead even if Queensland recover to record a outright victory, worth six points.
Queensland and New South Wales are locked together in third place in the Shield standings on 22 points.
